summary: APPROVE. Readiness-check mode on scripts/install_constellation.py verified independently against every Close Criteria item: four separately-callable, separately-tested check functions (engine-runnable via sys.executable distinguishing interpreter-missing/pytest-missing/working; work-area-present via .git as dir-or-file; skills-installed via CORPUS.json plus expected-skill-folder membership; hooks-shippable reusing detect_hook_wiring plus git-ls-files tracked-ness, scoped correctly between project and user), combined by a thin CLI layer that reports and refuses with a named per-item reason and exits 0 only when every targeted agent is fully ready. Read every new function myself rather than trusting the grep-based wiring claim: settings.json is written at exactly one place in the file, inside wire_hooks(), structurally unreachable from the --check-readiness branch, which also explicitly rejects --wire-hooks/--baseline-only combinations up front. Reproduced both required pytest runs myself (25/25, 132/132/380 subtests). Went beyond restating the implementer's evidence: mutation-tested the load-bearing interpreter-vs-pytest discrimination case against a deliberately-broken always-ready stand-in and confirmed the guarding test genuinely fails, and ran the CLI itself end-to-end against a real fresh git-init'd project and a real never-installed target outside the test suite. Diff scope is exactly the two allowed files; the specific exclusions (checklist_engine.py, test_checklist_engine.py) are absent, as required. Fowler pass: 12/12 baseline smells rendered, 0 flagged, 2 overridden with logged repo-standard reasons, verify_fowler_pass.py exits 0. Zero blocking findings. One real, already-acknowledged, explicitly out-of-scope gap raised as a triage candidate: README.md's Install section does not yet mention --check-readiness (the implementer correctly left it untouched since README.md was not in this gate's Allowed Scope).
triage_candidates: README.md's Install section documents --wire-hooks and --baseline-only but not the new --check-readiness flag; a future doc pass should add a one-line mention. Not a blocker -- README.md was outside this gate's Allowed Scope.
workflow_feedback: Handoff was precise and actionable end to end -- Close Criteria, Allowed Scope, Specific Exclusions, and Required Evidence all mapped directly onto concrete, checkable things. One minor friction: the handoff's Required Evidence names 'python -m pytest tests/test_install_constellation.py -k readiness -q' but IMPLEMENTER_RESULT's own headline evidence ran against the whole tests/ directory instead, producing a different deselected-count that could read as a discrepancy on a quick diff of numbers; worth noting in this gate's evidence that the pass count (25) matched even though the denominator did not, so a future reviewer doesn't waste time chasing a mismatch that isn't one. Engine mechanics: REVIEW_SURVEY.template.json's r6-fowler item ships with 'templates/FOWLER_PASS.template.json' as its literal check command path in the imperative text, but the actual postcondition c1 (which is what advance/record gates on) already carries the real resolved path as a placeholder to fill at instantiation -- that's the documented normal path and worked cleanly once I substituted it; flagging only because the imperative prose and the postcondition disagree in wording (template path vs. instance path) in a way a less careful reader could stumble on.
